chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabie, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A Muslim is a brother of a Muslim; he does not oppress him, nor abandon him, nor backbite him, nor deceive him, nor deprive him.'

Rabie said: 'A man from our companions asked me in Al-Madina, saying, "I heard Fuzayl saying that." I said to him, "Yes." He said, "For I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: A Muslim is a brother of a Muslim; he does not oppress him, nor deceive him, nor abandon him, nor backbite him, nor betray him, nor deprive him."'
ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical duties of a Muslim towards their brother in faith according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi underscores the comprehensive nature of Islamic brotherhood by listing six specific prohibitions—oppression, abandonment, backbiting, deception, betrayal, and deprivation—that define the moral bond between believers. The inclusion of a secondary chain of transmission via a companion in Medina highlights the widespread acceptance and consistency of these ethical standards within early Shia scholarly circles. Practically, it serves as a foundational code of conduct for maintaining social cohesion and trust within the community of the Momineen.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘A Muslim is a brother of a Muslim, neither oppressing him, nor abandoning him, nor backbiting him, nor deceiving him, nor depriving him’.

Rabi’e said, ‘So a man from our companions asked me at Al-Medina saying, ‘I heard Fuzayl saying that’. So I said, ‘Yes’. So he said, ‘But I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘A Muslim is a brother of a Muslim, neither oppressing him, nor deceiving him, nor abandoning him, nor backbiting him, nor betraying him, nor depriving him’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma’il from Fadl ibn Shadhan all from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Rib’i from Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim. He does not do injustice to him, does not betray him, does not speak ill of one behind his back, does not violate his trust and does not deprive him.’
Rib’i has said, ‘Certain individuals of our people asked me in Madina saying, “I have heard Fudayl saying what just you said.” I then said to him, ‘Yes, it is true.’

He then said, ‘I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, “A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim. He does not do injustice to him, does not deceive him, does not betray him, does not speak ill of one behind his back, does not violate his trust and does not deprive him.’”
